title: Firefox saved logins
whyItMatters: Lists every site, username and (encrypted) password Firefox saved. With the key file from the same profile, a stranger can recover the passwords themselves.
source: Mozilla Support, profiles where Firefox stores user data (logins.json): https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-firefox-stores-user-data
notes: Passwords are encrypted with the key in key4.db in the same profile, so the two files should be read together. Pair rule: browser.firefox.key4.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Firefox, open Settings > Privacy & Security > Logins and Passwords and use Export logins to save them to a file you keep.
cleanup.signOut: In Firefox, open the account menu and sign out of your Mozilla account, then choose to delete synced data from this device.
steps: In Firefox, remove the saved logins you no longer need from Logins and Passwords.
Delete the login file named in the plan if it is still there.
cleanup.risk: Without the export, every login saved in Firefox is lost; the encrypted passwords are only usable with the key file from the same profile.
cleanup.source: Mozilla Support, Password Manager - Remember, delete and edit logins and passwords in Firefox: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/password-manager-remember-delete-edit-logins
